Gospel singer Nathaniel Bassey said he is building subsidised apartments for his musicians and staff, with beneficiaries expected to move into their homes by Christmas. Bassey disclosed this in an Instagram post on Thursday, explaining that the housing scheme was designed to help members of his team own homes rather than continue renting. Bassey accompanied the announcement with a photograph of the apartment development. He said the beneficiaries would contribute a significant portion of the cost but would receive substantial subsidies. The singer said the project was funded partly through his personal investments, with his family providing land for the development. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “So, I had this idea of a housing scheme for our staff. “They would contribute a significant portion, but they would be highly subsidised. “I offered our family plot, put in funds and, in addition, my friend, Mr Peter Chubby of Danville Mall, agreed to a joint venture arrangement. (Please thank him for us!) We started building by faith, little by little, one block here and another block there,” he said. Four govs attend Adeboye’s crusade in Delta Ibi Dave records 10 gospel songs in Gombe after US, UK tours Tope Alabi, Testimony Jaga, others for Praise in the City He said the project had taught him that musicians could successfully organise themselves and commit to long-term goals when given proper guidance. “One thing I realised doing this was that we used to be told musicians were not organised. But with the right guidance, they can do great things. They have committed to this. See, you never know what you can do until you try. “Men and brethren, by Christmas, imagine my joy seeing them in their apartment (fully owned), with their children swinging at the play area. Truly, the real blessing is being a blessing,” he wrote. Bassey said the development was the first phase of a wider plan, adding that he hoped to share the experience with other creatives and musicians in the Christian community to encourage them to pursue similar housing initiatives. He also reflected on the responsibility of leadership, saying leaders should ensure that those around them benefit when they achieve success. “Finally, as a leader, if you are the only one sharing testimonies, after a while, those around you will soon be despondent. Make sure as God lifts you, you carry them along,” he added. Nathaniel Bassey is a Nigerian gospel singer, trumpeter, songwriter and pastor known for gospel songs including Imela, Onise Iyanu and Olowogbogboro. He has also gained international attention through Hallelujah Challenge, an online prayer and praise gathering he initiated in 2017, which attracts participants from different countries. Okiki Adeduyite Okiki is a journalist with over seven years experience covering politics, foreign news, society, entertainment and the film industry.
